name: Douglas Waters
life: “I still remember a letter addressed to somebody who didn't own my room anymore.” People around the window at Night Shift Donuts know Douglas by a small Monday habit. Douglas knows when the going-home crowd and the coming-to-work crowd will both be there.
voice: I rented his old room. The first letter that arrived asked my permission to send another.
appearance: Douglas has a wide brow and a narrow jaw. Look for thick, tightly coiled hair. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a gray fisher's sweater with a train token tied to a zipper pull. In conversation Douglas steadies a cup with both hands while listening.
personality: Douglas is cheerful on a bad morning and unexpectedly melancholy after a success. Finishing a hard thing means losing the daily company of the people who worked on it.
agenda: To give a clear answer about receiving more forwarded mail.
family: Rafael Sloan is Douglas’s cousin raised in the same household. Douglas chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. Rafael brings a spare shopping bag. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *The crane shadow*, Rafael says, “I spent my first year here looking down. This gull was the first thing that made me look up.”
connections: Lou Reed. Two households sort out where letters ought to go without making a public forwarding list.

reactions.situation: The returning father asks to visit the old address
reactions.response: Douglas checks whether the person living there now wants visitors.
